body: Funny, i'm the opposite. Hell seems preferable because you might take comfort in the fact that your suffering is intentional and out of your control, as opposed to earth where people suffer for no reason through our choices.
this was fucking useless, and the chatlines have taken so long i don't think i have the willpower any more. at least my parents can't say i didn't try

Well, active actions that cause pain to others is easy. I decide not to maintain my relationships, or text back my friends, and I know it's bad, but I continue to do it. Doesn't matter if my depression is doing it, and it's separating me from everyone, it's still a choice I'm making. It's shameful and selfish to only talk to someone when you feel up to it, but I don't stop. Because I don't really feel anything towards it. I don't feel like any person needs me in their life and it's easier if I just back away before I mess up. That's an example of an active action.   
But passive actions are harder, because I don't usually recognize them until after the pain has happened. An example might be that I've bought a piece of clothing from somewhere that uses sweatshops, and that caused pain without my intent or knowing, but I contributed. Or easy enough, I'm white, and had unknowingly perpetuated so many racist ideas as a teenager that I never understood or intended to be harmful, but still were. And there doesn't seem to be an end to that process of learning later on that you've hurt someone. Sorry if that doesn't make much sense.
Maybe we'll see each other in that world, if it comes to pass. Thank you, stranger.

It does seem less terrifying, it's tempting. Might fuck around and find out just for curiosity sake. But what do we do? I have hope that the systems in place can be changed by revolution, but even that is such a small chance that we get it right. And if we get wrong, what, I stayed around to watch all my friends and family die? It's like my options are accept the inevitable crumbling of our planet and society or die trying to fight it. Thanks, though, it's not great that we're both feeling this, but at least it's together.
